scope: devices/catalogue-batch vs origin/main - 31 changed device paths (27 devices added, 1 duplicate removed, 2 panels converted to pass-through)
method: Scripted consistency pass over every changed spec: vendor/model/label present, category in the palette's known set, sourceUrl https, description and notes non-trivial, expandInterfaces() name uniqueness, declared speed present in speedCaps, PoE ports backed by a budget and the poe-pse capability. Then a behavioural check on anything the script flagged.

findings.what: Every PoE-sourcing NVR lacks the 'poe-pse' capability: amcrest/NV4108E-HS, axis/S3008, dahua/NVR5216-16P-EI2, dahua/NVR5216-16P-4KS2E, dahua/NVR5232-16P-4KS2E, hikvision/DS-7616NI-K2/16P, hikvision/DS-7608NI-K2/8P, reolink/RLN8-410, uniview/NVR301-08X-P8, vivotek/ND9425P.
findings.evidence: 202 devices carry PoE-out ports or a budget; 153 declare poe-pse. The NVR category is uniformly in the other 49. Checked whether it breaks anything: it does not - the simulator resolves PoE from poeBudget, and a Dahua camera on dahua/NVR5232-16P-4KS2E PoE 1 reports powered: true, draw 12.95 W against a 130 W budget, and the same on uniview/NVR301-08X-P8 against 75 W.
findings.action: Left alone. Adding the capability to the two NVRs I added would make them inconsistent with the nine already in the tree, and the flag has no behavioural effect here. Worth one deliberate pass across all 49 if the capability is meant to be authoritative.

findings.severity: false positive in my own review script
findings.what: The PON splitters (prysmian XSPSG00009/00010/00054, commscope SP-11600S2S2CAAA) declare speed '10G' with speedCaps [1244, 2488, 9953] - GPON/XGS-PON line rates, deliberately not 10000.
findings.evidence: Their ports are type 'pon', not 'ethernet', and the caps are the PON rates from the datasheets. A review rule that maps a '10G' port speed to 10000 Mbps does not apply to a PON leg.
findings.action: No change to the data; the rule needs a pon exemption if it is ever promoted from a review script to a real audit.

findings.what: fs/FHD-1U-PP-24LC had no notes at all, and it was one of the two devices whose behaviour this branch changed (it gained port pairs).
findings.evidence: The file carried vendor/model/label/description/sourceUrl and nothing else; the pass-through claim was therefore only visible in the engine.
findings.action: Added notes recording the 0.2 dB insertion loss, the 96-fibre enclosure, and that the panel is now paired so a run can cross the ODF instead of terminating on it.

findings.what: All 27 added specs pass the structural checks: unique port names, declared speed inside speedCaps, https source, real description and notes, known category, PoE ports backed by a budget.
findings.evidence: Script output: 31 paths, the only per-file lines were the three findings above.
